name: Beckman glass-electrode acidimeter
summary: In 1935 National Technical Laboratories sold Arnold Beckman's acidimeter, a vacuum-tube meter reading a glass electrode, which made measuring acidity quick and routine in laboratories.
description: Early National Technical Laboratories glass-electrode vacuum-tube pH/acidimeter sold to laboratory customers.

impact.note: Made an existing measurement quick and routine in laboratories and opened the line of electronic chemical instruments. Total implies tier 2, not the reviewed 1.

why: A California citrus-products laboratory needed a sturdy way to measure the acidity of lemon juice, and glass electrodes gave currents too small for ordinary meters.
